must_fix.title: HEAD responses lose Content-Length under ETag
must_fix.evidence: finish() in middleware/etag.go only writes the buffered body for GET, so net/http never computes Content-Length for HEAD. Probe with httptest.NewServer and a handler doing w.Write([]byte("hello")): `go run ./zz_probe` -> `plain HEAD 200 CL: 5 5` vs `etag HEAD 200 CL: -1  "2cf24dba..."` (GET under ETag still has CL 5). No test covers HEAD Content-Length.

nits: A HEAD-only handler that writes no body and sets no Content-Length gets the empty-body ETag (e3b0...), which never matches the GET ETag; document this or skip computing the ETag.
`If-None-Match: *` gives no 304 when a 200 HEAD response has no ETag (the handler set Content-Length and wrote no body), although RFC 9110 says * matches any current representation.
Hijack sets hijacked=true before calling the underlying Hijack, so if that Hijack fails after a status was written, finish drops the buffered response without saying so.
For GET the body is fully buffered, so the middleware could set Content-Length instead of letting bodies over about 2 KB go out chunked.

report:
I found a HEAD regression, so I'm writing up the review now.

## Review: `middleware.ETag`

**Checks run:** `gofmt -l .` reports nothing. `go vet ./...` passes. `go test ./...` passes, and so does `go test -race -count=1 ./middleware/`. The README row and link are in the right places, next to the other entries. The repo doesn't add per-change entries to its CHANGELOG, so this PR doesn't need one.

The If-None-Match parsing behaves correctly: weak comparison, lists spread over several header lines, `*`, the allowed etag characters, and stopping at a malformed member. Other methods and non-200 statuses pass through unchanged, and a 304 drops the representation headers.

### Must fix

**HEAD responses lose their `Content-Length` (regression).** Without the middleware, when a handler writes a body for a HEAD request, net/http works out the `Content-Length` from what was written. That covers both the `GetHead` setup and plain handlers. `finish` (`middleware/etag.go`, the `if r.Method == http.MethodGet && w.body.Len() > 0` branch) never forwards the buffered body for HEAD, so net/http never sees a length. Instead of carrying the same headers as GET, the HEAD response now has none.

I checked this with a temporary probe package in the repo (since removed). It serves `w.Write([]byte("hello"))` through `httptest.NewServer`, once bare and once wrapped in `ETag`:

```
$ go run ./zz_probe
plain GET 200 CL: 5 5
plain HEAD 200 CL: 5 5
etag GET 200 CL: 5 5 "2cf24dba…9824"
etag HEAD 200 CL: -1  "2cf24dba…9824"
```

Since the body is fully buffered, the fix is to set `Content-Length` from `w.body.Len()` when the handler hasn't set it, at least for HEAD. A test should cover this. `TestETagHeadWithGetHandler` only checks the ETag and the empty body.

### Nits

- If a HEAD-specific handler writes no body and sets no `Content-Length`, it gets the ETag of an empty body (`e3b0…`). That doesn't match the GET representation, so an If-None-Match carrying the GET's ETag never gives a 304 on HEAD. The doc comment could say so.
- When a HEAD response has no ETag (the handler set a non-zero `Content-Length` and wrote no body), `If-None-Match: *` doesn't produce a 304. RFC 9110 says `*` matches whenever a current representation exists.
- `Hijack` sets `w.hijacked = true` before calling `hj.Hijack()`. If the underlying Hijack fails after a status was written, `finish` then drops the buffered response without saying so.
- For GET, the body is already fully buffered, so the middleware could set `Content-Length` instead of letting bodies over about 2 KB go out chunked.
